faq.q: How did the Treaty of Versailles lead to World War Two?
faq.a: Many Germans saw it as harsh and humiliating. Hitler promised to tear it up, win back lost land and rebuild the army, which won him support. Historians debate how much the treaty itself was to blame.
asks: Did Versailles cause World War Two?

faq.q: How did the Great Depression help Hitler?
faq.a: From 1929, mass unemployment and poverty made people lose faith in democratic governments. In Germany, the Nazis grew from a small party to the largest in parliament by 1932.
asks: Why did people vote for the Nazis?

faq.q: Who were the dictators of the 1930s?
faq.a: Adolf Hitler in Germany, Benito Mussolini in Italy, and military leaders in Japan built aggressive, expanding states. Joseph Stalin ruled the Soviet Union as a dictator too.

The policy, led by British prime minister Neville Chamberlain, of giving in to some of Hitler's demands to avoid war, as at the Munich Agreement in 1938. Supporters said Britain needed time to rearm; critics said it encouraged Hitler.

faq.q: When did World War Two start?
faq.a: In Europe it began on 1 September 1939, when Germany invaded Poland; Britain and France declared war on 3 September. In Asia, many date it from Japan's full invasion of China in 1937.

facts: Britain and France declared war on Germany on 3 September 1939.
The Munich Agreement was signed in September 1938.

quiz.say: Which event started the war in Europe in 1939?
quiz.show: The war in Europe began when…

wrong.1: The Wall Street Crash was in 1929; it caused hard times, not the war itself.
wrong.2: The Treaty of Versailles was signed in 1919.

quiz.why: Britain and France gave Hitler some of what he wanted, hoping to avoid war.

wrong.1: Appeasement was the opposite of declaring war.
wrong.2: It was a policy, not a building project.
